interactions.label: Trace architecture
interactions.teaches: The DCGAN is two mirrored convolutional pipelines: the generator expands a compact latent vector into an image, while the discriminator compresses an image into a single real/fake probability.

demo_steps.title: Overview: two mirrored pipelines
demo_steps.narration: The left underbrace marks the Generator and the right underbrace marks the Discriminator. The block proportions show the main symmetry: spatial size grows in the generator and shrinks in the discriminator, while channel depth changes in the opposite direction.

demo_steps.title: Generator: expand z into an image
demo_steps.narration: The highlighted path starts at the 100×1 latent variable z, projects and reshapes it into 4×4×1024, then uses fractional convolutions to upsample through 8×8×512, 16×16×256, and 32×32×128.

demo_steps.title: Image handoff: x or x*
demo_steps.narration: The generator output is a 64×64×3 image. The same discriminator input position represents either a real image x or a generated image x*, matching the label on the central arrow.

demo_steps.title: Discriminator: compress the image
demo_steps.narration: The highlighted discriminator path applies strided convolutions that reduce spatial resolution from 64×64 to 32×32, 16×16, 8×8, and 4×4, while increasing feature depth up to 1024 channels.

demo_steps.title: Final decision
demo_steps.narration: A final 4×4 convolution collapses the 4×4×1024 volume to a 1×1 scalar, and the fixed sigmoid activation converts that scalar into Pr(real).

authoredPrompt: This figure shows the complete DCGAN (Deep Convolutional Generative Adversarial Network) architecture as two mirrored pipelines labeled Generator (left) and Discriminator (right), each spanning one half of the figure and delineated by underbrace annotations. The Generator begins with a 100×1 latent variable z, passes it through a “Project and reshape” step to produce a 4×4×1024 feature volume, and then applies a series of fractional (transposed) convolutions with arctan activations that progressively upsample through 8×8×512, 16×16×256, 32×32×128, and finally a 64×64×3 output image. The Discriminator receives either a real image x or a generated image x*, starting at 64×64×3, and uses strided convolutions to downsample through 32×32×128, 16×16×256, 8×8×512, 4×4×1024, before a 4×4 convolution collapses the spatial dimensions to a 1×1 scalar that is passed through a sigmoid activation to produce the probability Pr(real). All feature volumes are rendered as three-dimensional orange-shaded parallelogram blocks, with black arrows indicating data flow. This figure introduces the DCGAN architecture, which replaces fully connected hidden layers with purely convolutional operations to produce and evaluate photorealistic images.
authoredInteractions:
- Animate the generator forward pass: trace the latent variable z (100×1 noise vector) through Project and reshape, then through fractional convolution stages watching the tensor grow from 4×4×1024 to 8×8×512 to 16×16×256 to 32×32×128 to the final 64×64×3 output image
- Animate the discriminator forward pass: trace a real or generated image x through strided convolution stages from 64×64×3 down to 4×4×1024, then to the 1×1 output and through sigmoid to Pr(real)
- Toggle between sigmoid and arctan final activation: highlight the discriminator's output block and show how each function shapes the probability score range, updating the Pr(real) label

interactions.label: Animate generator forward pass
interactions.teaches: The generator starts from a compact 100-dimensional latent vector and progressively expands spatial resolution while reducing channel depth, ending in a 64×64×3 image.

interactions.label: Animate discriminator forward pass
interactions.teaches: The discriminator reverses the generator’s spatial expansion: strided convolutions compress the image into deeper feature volumes and finally into a single real/fake probability.

interactions.label: Final activation
interactions.teaches: Different bounded nonlinearities convert the discriminator’s final scalar logit into an interpretable score; sigmoid gives the standard probability-shaped mapping, while normalized arctan gives a gentler bounded alternative.

demo_steps.title: Generator expands noise into an image
demo_steps.narration: Play the generator pass. The highlight begins at the 100×1 latent vector, then steps through 4×4×1024, 8×8×512, 16×16×256, 32×32×128, and finally the 64×64×3 image.

demo_steps.title: Discriminator compresses an image into a decision
demo_steps.narration: Play the discriminator pass. The input image x or x* is reduced through 32×32×128, 16×16×256, 8×8×512, and 4×4×1024 before the 4×4 convolution produces a 1×1 scalar.

demo_steps.title: Compare output nonlinearities
demo_steps.narration: Switch the final activation from sigmoid to arctan. The output block remains the same 1×1 scalar source, but the displayed curve and Pr(real) label update to show the chosen score mapping.

discrepancies: The discriminator output includes an extra sigmoid/arctan inset graph that is not present in the source figure.
The generated layout is horizontally compressed, causing several tensor labels and operation labels to overlap or crowd the blocks compared with the clean spacing in the source.
The discriminator final activation is made switchable to arctan, whereas the source shows arctan only at the generator output and sigmoid at the discriminator output.
Several block proportions and separations are off, especially in the discriminator where the 32×32, 16×16, 8×8, and 4×4 volumes are too tightly packed.
The generated image plane is a generic pixelated texture and does not closely resemble the source image patch, though it conveys the intended 64×64×3 output.
evaluation.notes: The main GAN architecture is recognizable with most blocks, arrows, braces, colors, and labels present, but the figure is crowded and adds a misleading activation-toggle/inset not in the source.

Remove the extra activation inset graph unless it is explicitly required, since it is not part of the source figure.

Adjust block sizes and positions, especially in the discriminator, to better match the source proportions and separation.
